## Design

### 2026-10-25 – This was just research into my project. i want to do an idea where you can record different instruments and play them back etc. I could do this using peizo buzzers for the drums etc.

**0.85h**

This was just research into my project. i want to do an idea where you can record different instruments and play them back etc. I could do this using peizo buzzers for the drums etc.

how can i store data?
SD card module
How can i send data?
i could use a 3.2mm jack module

Converting MP3 files to being playable, i need a music module:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/427hODD7h4ylsfNe58I5XNpn8qGPPHsr/1aeec1866be120ab7871fcce3dbbbf9641e511bd3362708a21ddd1b8c3ecdb2e.png)

I may also need an Amp to boost music.
I need 4 buttons to record, stop, play and delete
Here i looked at how i could approach the project:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/427hODD7h4ylsfNe58I5XNpn8qGPPHsr/38e7a0d1624e832dc22a5b337e9d83317e92129d5806782cdbfd17cbf74451ac.png)

So in summary , I could use MP3 files to store the sound notes of individual notes , use a music module to convert them and I can store these notes in the sd card to be replayed.

### 2026-10-25 – After a bit of thinking, i might use the midi-project as a base and continue on with my ideas.

**2.85h**

After a bit of thinking, i might use the midi-project as a base and continue on with my ideas.
My thoughts that I think if i use the rotary encoder to change between different instruments i can create a multi-instrument melody.

Time- 1hr 30min - time i spent on the schematic

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/427hODD7h4ylsfNe58I5XNpn8qGPPHsr/41fd1231ea2eed54d8b43844e4f1e2440b098ea475d2d17a07e8d8d28c293dfb.png)

I just added the schematic and went along with the diagram making a few changes here and there. I decided not to use sliders as i wasn't sure it would be in my budget.
In my first design , i researched and thought about using a 3.5mm jack port to connect to a speaker. Upon reviewing the code , this wouldn't have worked as the code makes the esp32-S3-Zero act as a midi controller (I think), so i would have to use a computer or something. I also may of not had enough ports

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/427hODD7h4ylsfNe58I5XNpn8qGPPHsr/723ebd3a759126115aaf94d3ebb8c070cc71505566d5491ebeba67b291403471.png)
If I follow my current idea, i can use the rotary encoder to spin and switch between my different instruments.
Current thought:
I may also add a second one to control the volume

Time: 1h 21 min
Spent the time connecting the wires and components, placing them and creating a board
(Update from the future, another problem which occurred was i was in the wrong units (mil) and i was panicking a bit to why my pcb was so much over 100"mm" which would increase the costs.)
